title: R Shiny Apps
text:
These apps run on your machine



Every R package listed here includes a Shiny app. The apps run locally in R — install the package from CRAN and launch from your console. There is no hosted version: the service that previously hosted these apps is no longer under my control, so rather than ship links that fail, each card below gives you the exact command.

title: R Shiny Apps
text:
Regression and modeling




olsrr
Build linear regression models and iterate through specifications quickly. Produces full olsrr model output from the UI.
install.packages("olsrr")
olsrr::ols_launch_app()







blorr
Build, validate and monitor binary logistic regression models with comprehensive output, model fit and validation statistics.
install.packages("blorr")
blorr::blr_launch_app()







xplorerr
One app, seven entry points. Linear and logistic regression, descriptive statistics, inference, RFM analysis, distributions and the visualizer.
install.packages("xplorerr")
xplorerr::app_linear_regression()
Also available: app_descriptive(), app_visualizer(), app_logistic_regression(), app_inference(), app_rfm_analysis(), app_vistributions().

title: R Shiny Apps
text:
Statistics




descriptr
Generate and visualize descriptive statistics for numeric and categorical data. Explore key statistical distributions with interactive plots.
install.packages("descriptr")
descriptr::ds_launch_shiny_app()







inferr
Beginner-friendly hypothesis testing with parametric and non-parametric tests, flexible input options and structured results.
install.packages("inferr")
inferr::ifr_launch_shiny_app()







vistributions
Visualize probability distributions and run statistical quality checks on univariate data.
install.packages("vistributions")
vistributions::vdist_launch_app()

title: R Shiny Apps
text:
Customer analytics




rfm
Customer segmentation using recency, frequency and monetary value analysis. Build customized segments from customer- or transaction-level data.
install.packages("rfm")
rfm::rfm_launch_app()









nse2r has no app



nse2r exported an nse_app() Shiny entry point, but the package was archived on CRAN on 2023-08-07 and is under revival, so it is deliberately excluded from this page rather than shipped with a command that cannot be run. See Packages for its current status.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
I build statistical software that holds up outside a tutorial, and I help teams do the same. My work sits where R, statistics, economics and finance overlap — regression diagnostics, customer segmentation, descriptive and inferential statistics, and the unglamorous plumbing that keeps an analysis reproducible six months later when someone else has to rerun it.
Most of that work is open source. The package portfolio below is used far more widely than I expected when I started writing it, and it is the reason people find their way here: the packages are free, the vignettes are free, and there is no upsell attached to any of it.
I also write. Six data science textbooks are free to read online, and I founded Rsquared Academy, an open-source education platform for data science, where the courses behind those books live.
I earned my postgraduate degree from Madras School of Economics (Anna University), Chennai, and now maintain the portfolio independently from Bengaluru, India.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
Teaching
I run Rsquared Academy, where the courses behind the books are taught in full. It is an open-source education platform, not a lead-generation funnel — the course material is written to be useful even if you never sign up for anything.

For individuals. Self-paced and live courses on R, the tidyverse, visualization, SQL and command-line tooling.
For teams. Masterclasses built around your own data and problems, run as hands-on sessions rather than lectures.

title: Hey, I am Aravind
text:
Consulting & Advisory
Model validation and econometric audits. Independent review of specification, identification and inference — for teams who inherited a model and need to know whether it is defensible. You get a written report, not just a corrected script.
Custom package development and architecture. Internal R or Python tooling built to survive handover: documented, tested, and structured so your team can extend it without me. Most consulting work is undocumented code that one person understands, and that is a single point of failure I can help remove.
Team masterclasses. Tidyverse, SQL, command-line tooling. Built around your data, your conventions and your team’s existing stack.
Who this is for: teams shipping quantitative work that other people have to maintain. Who it is not for: one-off analyses, or anyone looking for a pre-packaged answer.

title: E-Books
text:
About these books
They were authored to supplement the courses at Rsquared Academy. Some are beginner friendly while others assume prior familiarity with a topic.
They began as blog posts, expanded into tutorials, and were eventually rewritten into short books with the sharp edges filed off. The style is deliberately plain — short chapters, worked examples, and the parts of the documentation people usually skip.
None of them replaces the official R documentation. If you want one place to start, Introduction to R is the one.
If these were useful, the courses behind them are at rsquaredacademy.com.
